reconstructed_theorem_text: E_n=EuclideanSpace R (Fin(n+1)), the real (n+1)-coordinate space with its l2 Euclidean norm. Let S_n={z in E_n: ||z||=1}, considered as a subtype when it is used as a carrier. For a function a:S_n -> A into a type with a distinguished zero, write R(a)(z)=0 if z=0 and R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) otherwise; normalization is the first component of the supplied H. For A:E_n->E_n, coordinateDivergence A(z)=sum_(k in Fin(n+1)) lineDeriv_R (y -> (A(y))_k) z e_k, using the standard coordinate vectors e_k. The supplied trace formula is conditional on A being differentiable at z. For each n and every V:S_n->E_n, this target defines the real function x -> coordinateDivergence(R(V))(x) on S_n. Equivalently, at unit x it sums the kth ambient-coordinate line derivative of R(V) in direction e_k over k in Fin(n+1). V need not be tangent or differentiable in the declaration. No derivative-existence or independent intrinsic-divergence identification is asserted; the trace characterization may only be used under its own differentiability condition.
objects: An arbitrary sphere-to-ambient vector map V, its radial extension and ambient coordinate divergence restricted to S_n.
quantifiers: Implicit n, then V, then x.
assumptions: No tangency, smoothness or integrability premise.
conclusion: Defined scalar: sum_k lineDeriv_R (z -> R(V)(z)_k) x e_k.
scopes: Literal coordinate derivative sum at a unit point; a trace-of-Frechet-derivative identification is conditional, not unconditional.
constant_dependencies: Sum over n+1 standard ambient coordinate directions, with no average or dimension normalization.
